direct_reception_checks.witness: Augustine, Enarrationes XVI §§1–14; XXXII §§1–22; XCV §§1–15; NPNF headings XVII, XXXIII, XCVI
direct_reception_checks.outcome: Three complete retained English expositions read. Christ-and-body speaker, prior hearing, wings of mercy, grace and nourishment, universal new song, humility and judgment support the dossier. Anti-Donatist and other historical polemics remain bounded; the wood variant is reception, not appointed wording.

direct_reception_checks.witness: Jerome, In Isaiam XII on 44:28–45:7; DCO Pars 3 pp.126–129
direct_reception_checks.outcome: All four exact pages image-inspected through the book XIII boundary. Cyrus is the literal Persian king, while a Christological type remains possible. His ignorance prevents direct identification with the Son; the gifted-teacher application credits the giver. Modern typesetting and unidentified historical exemplar remain explicit.

Exact retained HTML anchors extracted and read. Checked Cyrus and recognition, literal tribute versus mystical image, election evidenced by effects, divine willing with free agency, participated light, protective wings, and bodily/spiritual/sacramental nourishment with fear and hope.

direct_reception_checks.witness: Chrysostom, Matthew LXX §§1–2; LXV §§4–5; Philippians VIII; 1 Thessalonians I on 1:1–7
direct_reception_checks.outcome: Retained NPNF text read at the direct exegesis and relevant adjacent argument. Real civic dues are qualified by godliness; humility opposes ambition; work/labour/endurance remain active. Matthew 20:28 is identified as a parallel to Mark. The Philippians word-of-life gloss is distinguished from the NPNF editor’s disagreement.

direct_reception_checks.witness: Bede, In Marci III, PL 92 (1862), cols.235–236, especially 236A–B; complete Latin derivative at Mark 10
direct_reception_checks.outcome: Exact retained print leaf image read and compared with the derivative. Blood given for the world and willing believers in the many gloss are both retained. The source does not independently establish a Greek lexical conclusion or a grace-free origin of faith.

direct_reception_checks.witness: Gregory Nazianzen, Oration XLV §§21–24, especially22; Aquinas, Summa III.48.4
direct_reception_checks.outcome: Exact retained public-domain English passages read. Both refuse the devil’s entitlement; Gregory’s acceptance/incarnation account and Aquinas’s payment/satisfaction account remain positively different. Gutenberg’s fourth-article heading typo is not adopted as a locus.
Complete official catechesis checked. It labels cross interpretation as Christian rereading and directly invokes Mark 10:43–45; it establishes reception, not this Sunday’s appointment.

consequential_difficulty_tests.test: Does divine use of Cyrus make him Jesus or sanctify all civil authority?
consequential_difficulty_tests.actual_locus: Jerome, In Isaiam XII, DCO Pars3 pp.127–128; Chrysostom, Matthew LXX §§1–2
consequential_difficulty_tests.outcome: No. The literal referent and his failure to know God remain; the Gospel witness limits dues by godliness. Reading A’s qualified instrumentality and civic obligation survive this test.

consequential_difficulty_tests.test: Does gift-first theology erase freely enacted service or make faith self-originating?
consequential_difficulty_tests.actual_locus: Aquinas, Philippians 2 lectio3, paragraph87838; Chrysostom, 1 Thessalonians I on 1:3–5; Bede, Mark III, PL92 col.236B
consequential_difficulty_tests.outcome: No. Aquinas explicitly guards divine inward action and human agency; Chrysostom gives costly action content; Bede supplies willing reception without independently explaining its origin. Reading B keeps these distinct contributions rather than merging them into an unsupported formula.

consequential_difficulty_tests.test: Can the psalm cross or world-stability language be represented as the sung appointment?
consequential_difficulty_tests.actual_locus: OLM145A, printed79; actual USCCB Psalm strophe; Augustine XCV §11; John Paul II audience §5
consequential_difficulty_tests.outcome: No. The omitted clause and ancient wood variant stay outside the appointed wording. Both editorial readings preserve that limit.

interpretation_assessment.outcome: Both are developed, materially distinct editorial readings of the full formulary. A asks about real earthly obligations under divine sovereignty; B asks how received gifts form willing, fruitful service. Each gives all eleven keys a contribution and its own literal, allegorical, moral and anagogical argument. They are complementary, with no fabricated doctrinal conflict.

A: John Chrysostom: actual dues and the godliness limit
B: Thomas Aquinas: inward divine agency with free response and sacramental nourishment
John Chrysostom: costly faith, love, hope and willing service

interpretation_assessment.standing: Carrier identities and standing checked against the central author-standing inventory. Augustine and Bede supply further registered patristic support. No unverified liturgical commentator is used to carry a complete modern formulary.

chronology.place_and_scope_outcome: All twelve rows checked. The common composition boundary applies to all three Psalms; unresolved occasions group only Entrance and Communion Psalm. David’s era is attribution only. Temple restoration and Nativity are superscription/referent relations, not composition. Isaiah’s alternative frameworks do not date Cyrus’s conquest. Gospel composition is separate from the unresolved Matthew event and undated Mark saying. Corinth/Rome describe writing in the cited historical accounts; Thessalonica/Philippi identify recipients. Isaiah44:26–28, Matthew21:23–22:21 and Mark10:32–46 support the bounded narrative place phrases. No unsupported precise roadside locality is supplied.
